Position is actor[+0x2c/+0x30/+0x34], radius +0x1c, velocity +0x52. It builds the collision's fifth argument as actor[+0x1e] | ((actor[+0x28] & 0xc000) << 16), so the body height is in the low bits and the creature's own two bits land on 0x80000000 and 0x40000000 -- the pair collision opcode 0x18 tests. player_vertical passes a plain 0x6a4 with nothing on top

0x8004e094.name: actor_move_3d

0x80052e5c.name: actor_tick_driver
0x80052e5c.evidence: selects an actor, then runs 0x800500a8 over it; also copies an object record's position out of object_table into the actor at +0x2c

0x800500a8.name: actor_tick
0x800500a8.evidence: the per-frame creature machine: walks the 199 records of actor_table and switches on actor[+0xe] through the 241-arm table at 0x800128f0, guarded by `sltiu $v0, $v1, 0xf1`. Thirty arms are behaviours -- opcodes 0x00..0x1f without 0x07 and 0x08, plus 0x84 and 0xf0 -- and 209 opcodes reach 0x80052bf8, which calls level_hooks+0x24, the same escape into the level's own code the object machine has. It also reads a record at actor[+0x60] whose +0, +4 and +0xa it branches on. Confirmed live: a read of the running emulator on level 0 shows actor[+0xe] holding 6 on two active creatures and 0 on three others, which is the dispatch byte taking real values

0x8004dbc8.name: actor_move_horizontal
0x8004dbc8.evidence: the monsters' horizontal move, on current_actor rather than on the player: probes collision at the X- and Z-displaced positions, keeps the MAXIMUM floor (the lowest surface), and rejects the step when the feet would end more than 0x44c above it. Writes X to +0x2c and Z to +0x34; the vertical is actor_move_vertical. 0x8004dca0 is an inner label, not the entry

0x8002ed60.name: player_vertical
0x8002ed60.evidence: the player's height, a state machine on 0x801b25e8. Grounded it is a rate limiter towards the surface collide_surface leaves at 0x801e6474 -- 0x80/0x100/0x200 a frame, placed exactly inside 0x80, a fall past 0x400. States 0x10 and 0x40 are both falls, accelerating 0x50 and 0x28; 0x20 rises from -0x96 by 0xa; 0x50 is the landing recoil and falls through into state 0. emu/bp15.lua caught every store of the player's Y and all of them are in here; tools/movement.py picks the same instruction on 48 of 48

0x8002e3f8.name: player_horizontal

Called twice a frame from 0x8002fda0 and 0x8002fdb4, at the facing and a quarter turn off it

0x801b25e8.name: player_vstate

0x801b2656.name: player_vvel

0x801b2602.name: player_dy_applied

0x8002f9bc.name: player_walk

0x8002fe1c.name: player_turn

0x801b265c.name: buttons

0x801b2612.name: player_facing
0x801b2612.evidence: s16, 0x1000 to the turn. It is a quarter turn off the direction of travel: forward is player_horizontal at facing + 0x400 and strafing at facing, which the recording settled -- at facing 0 the game moves in +Z

0x801b2648.name: player_speed
0x801b2648.evidence: s16 forward speed. Accelerates by max/4 a frame while the button is held and decays by max/8 when it is not, clamping at zero by sign. The two rates differ, and a replay caught it: max/4 both ways overshot on 85 frames of a two-minute session, always while slowing down

0x801b264a.name: player_speed_mag
0x801b264a.evidence: isqrt(forward^2 + strafe^2), formed at 0x8002fd80; player_vertical tests it against 0xc9 when choosing a launch velocity

0x801b2664.name: player_speed_max

0x80081868.name: bind_forward
0x80081868.evidence: the first of fourteen u16 button masks, one per action; read by player_walk at 0x8002f9c8 and written by apply_control_scheme, which puts 0x1000 in it in all seven movement schemes. WITHDRAWN, the earlier entry here: it called this table key_bindings and read its masks against the raw hardware word, making 0x1000 TRIANGLE and 0x0800 R1. The two halves of that word are swapped by the time PadRead returns it, so 0x1000 is UP and 0x0800 is START. Four independent uses say so: the slot holding 0x0800 is read only by the pause menu, the one holding 0x0100 opens the map, play_movie skips a movie on 0x10/0x20/0x40/0x80 -- the four face buttons -- and everything on 0x800, and the title menu confirms on 0x20/0x40/0x800 and moves its cursor on 0x1000/0x4000. Under the raw reading those are, in order, R1 opening the menu, L2 the map, the four directions skipping a movie, and the cursor moving on TRIANGLE and CROSS

0x80076cc4.name: game_sin

0x80076da0.name: game_cos

0x80074508.name: game_isqrt

The walking step is speed^2/isqrt(speed^2), so that unit turns a speed of 200 into a step of 201, and a replay using an exact root disagreed with the game on 1394 frames of 3632 for that reason alone

0x80096150.name: isqrt_table

0x801b2652.name: player_bob_phase

0x801b2650.name: player_bob

0x8002f298.name: player_bob

_note_mo_wrapper.name: MO.T entry wrapper

Scanning the first 256 bytes for the TMD id found it only for the models that keep it near the front; 53 of level 0's 347 objects, the chests and statues among them, put it thousands of bytes in and were reported as having no model at all

0x801b2610.name: player_pitch

Found by logging nine candidates and recording one look up and down -- it was the only one that moved, over 136 values from -596 to +700, and it rests near -190. The first guess, 0x801b2614, reads zero for a whole session and is wrong. POSITIVE IS UP: the resting -190 was read as a downward tilt and the port was built on that, and a player looking up saw it look down

0x80040ae4.name: render_walk
0x80040ae4.evidence: two loops, not one. The first steps the ACTOR table at 0x80185da8 by 0x88 for 200 slots and draws a creature only when its +9 is 1; its model number is the mesh byte at +1 plus 0x80. The second steps object_table by 0x44 for 396 slots, skips a u16 type id of 0xff, clears bit 0x80 of +3 every frame and dispatches on the class byte at +4 -- 0xe9 and 0xe5 are skipped, 0x1f, 0xf0 and 0xf2 each have their own path. The old name here was object_walk, which described only the second half. For everything else the draw test is view_bits_at(position) & record +0, or type flag +3 bit 8 to draw regardless: every visible cell's view byte carries 2, which a placed record's +0 is, so an arm that zeroes +0 -- classes 0x0b, 0x14, 0x15, 0x1f, 0x59, 0x5f, 0xe0 to 0xe4, 0xe6, 0xe7 and 0xea, and whatever opcode 9 names -- hides the object. A creature is drawn by draw_model_plain with its angles +0x40, +0x42 + 0x800, +0x44 (0x80040c94) -- its model's front is -z -- or none at all for flag 0x20 (+0x28)

_note_object_model.name: object type -> model
_note_object_model.evidence: an object of type N uses MO.T[N + 128], and past MO.T's 428 entries the numbering continues into MOF.T. The 128 was MEASURED, not reasoned: a player stood in the game beside the port and named four pairs off the model gallery -- helmet type 34 = model 162, healing grass 104 = 232, save point 227 = 355, bull's head 253 = 381 -- and all four differ by exactly 128. The sizes agree: the grass is 384x211x416 under the rule where MO.T[type] gave it 4176x4096x3808, which is what the player saw as a big white thing. MO.T[type], the previous assumption, had never been checked against anything
